name: queensland_stratified
scope_note: 59 questions, a deliberate reduction from the MVP spec's ~100, scoped to what 6 papers can genuinely support. Documented as a dev-time scope choice in the same spirit as the spec's other stated shortcuts. The spec's 'temporal' stratum does not fit an academic-paper corpus (no time series), so it is substituted with temporal_provenance: publication years and the citation direction between papers, which are genuine time-ordered facts the corpus does contain. Unanswerable + false_premise = 11/59 (19%), matching the spec's ~20%.

questions.question: How many parameters does the GFM-RAG graph foundation model have?
questions.ground_truth: 8M parameters.

questions.question: How many knowledge graphs, triples and documents was GFM-RAG trained on?
questions.ground_truth: 60 knowledge graphs, over 14M triples, 700k documents.

questions.question: How many parameters does the G-reasoner graph foundation model have?
questions.ground_truth: 34M parameters.

questions.question: What is QuadGraph and how many layers does it have?
questions.ground_truth: A standardized four-layer abstraction unifying heterogeneous graph-structured knowledge.

questions.question: Which four benchmark datasets is ExpressGNN evaluated on?
questions.ground_truth: UW-CSE, Cora, synthetic Kinship, and FB15K-237.

questions.question: What two model families does ExpressGNN combine, and what does it use graph neural networks for?
questions.ground_truth: Markov Logic Networks and GNNs; GNNs perform variational inference in the MLN.

questions.question: What coverage and interval width improvements does QpiGNN report over its baselines?
questions.ground_truth: On average 22% higher coverage and 50% narrower intervals.

questions.question: What architecture does QpiGNN use to separate prediction from uncertainty estimation?
questions.ground_truth: A dual-head architecture decoupling prediction and uncertainty, trained with a quantile-free joint loss.

questions.question: Which Qwen3 model sizes are used in the OPSD experiments?
questions.ground_truth: Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B (instruct-tuned).

questions.question: In OPSD, what privileged information does the teacher policy condition on that the student does not see?
questions.ground_truth: Verified reasoning traces / ground-truth solutions; the student sees only the question.

questions.question: What loss does QpiGNN use to train its two heads?
questions.ground_truth: A quantile-free joint loss, with label-only supervision (no quantile inputs or post-processing).

questions.question: What task does QpiGNN target on graphs?
questions.ground_truth: Node regression - predicting target values for individual entities in graph-structured data.

questions.question: What stabilisation mechanism does OPSD introduce for training?
questions.ground_truth: A per-token pointwise KL clipping mechanism.

questions.question: Which training dataset does OPSD sample its mathematical reasoning problems from?
questions.ground_truth: The mathematical reasoning subset of OpenThoughts, up to 30K problem-solution pairs.

questions.question: What conference and year was ExpressGNN published at?
questions.ground_truth: ICLR 2020.

questions.question: What scalability techniques does G-reasoner implement for large-scale training?
questions.ground_truth: Mixed-precision training and a distributed message-passing mechanism across multiple GPUs.

questions.question: What problem does GFM-RAG say hinders existing GraphRAG performance?
questions.ground_truth: Noise and incompleteness within the graph structure.

questions.question: What assumption does QpiGNN say message passing commonly relies on but is rarely satisfied?
questions.ground_truth: Exchangeability.

questions.question: What inference problem in Markov Logic Networks motivates ExpressGNN?
questions.ground_truth: Inference in MLNs is computationally intensive, making industrial-scale application difficult.

questions.question: Which baseline reinforcement learning method is OPSD compared against?
questions.ground_truth: GRPO (and supervised fine-tuning).

questions.question: How many synthetic and real-world benchmarks is QpiGNN evaluated on?
questions.ground_truth: 19 benchmarks.

questions.question: What metric does OPSD report for accuracy on mathematical reasoning benchmarks?
questions.ground_truth: Avg@12 accuracy.

questions.question: Do GFM-RAG and G-reasoner share any authors?
questions.ground_truth: Yes - Linhao Luo, Zicheng Zhao, Chen Gong, Gholamreza Haffari, Dinh Phung and Shirui Pan appear on both.

questions.question: Which institution do the first authors of both GFM-RAG and G-reasoner belong to?
questions.ground_truth: Monash University (Linhao Luo), with Zicheng Zhao at NJUST on both.

questions.question: G-reasoner states a limitation of GFM-RAG. What is it, and how many parameters does the model it criticises have?
questions.ground_truth: GFM-RAG is limited to specific knowledge graphs and cannot generalize to other graph structures; it has 8M parameters.

questions.question: Which paper in this corpus evaluates on FB15K-237, and what inference technique does it use?
questions.ground_truth: ExpressGNN; it uses GNNs for variational inference in Markov Logic Networks.

questions.question: Which paper reports a 34M-parameter model, and what graph abstraction does that model consume?
questions.ground_truth: G-reasoner; it consumes QuadGraph, a four-layer unified abstraction.

questions.question: The paper that studies node regression uncertainty names a dual-head design. What are its two heads predicting?
questions.ground_truth: QpiGNN's dual heads predict the point estimate and the interval width separately.

questions.question: Which paper uses a single model as both teacher and student, and which model family does it experiment on?
questions.ground_truth: OPSD (Self-Distilled Reasoner); the Qwen3 family.

questions.question: Which paper was published at ICLR 2026, and how many benchmark datasets does it evaluate on?
questions.ground_truth: G-reasoner; six benchmark datasets.

questions.question: How does G-reasoner's parameter count compare with GFM-RAG's, and what limitation of GFM-RAG does G-reasoner set out to address?
questions.ground_truth: 34M vs 8M; GFM-RAG is limited to specific knowledge graphs and cannot generalize to other graph structures.

questions.question: Compare the graph representation used by GFM-RAG with the one used by G-reasoner.
questions.ground_truth: GFM-RAG reasons over a knowledge graph built from documents; G-reasoner unifies heterogeneous sources into QuadGraph, a four-layer abstraction.

questions.question: Both ExpressGNN and GFM-RAG claim their models generalize to knowledge graphs not seen during training. How does each describe that capability?
questions.ground_truth: ExpressGNN: GNN embeddings generalize to new entities or related KGs without retraining. GFM-RAG: first GFM applicable to unseen datasets without fine-tuning.

questions.question: What generation token caps are used for OPSD compared with GRPO?
questions.ground_truth: 1024 tokens for OPSD, 16k for GRPO.

questions.question: Contrast how GFM-RAG and G-reasoner each scale training to large datasets.
questions.ground_truth: GFM-RAG: two-stage training over 60 KGs/14M triples/700k docs. G-reasoner: mixed-precision training and distributed message-passing across GPUs.

questions.question: How does OPSD's token efficiency compare with GRPO's at the same number of training steps?
questions.ground_truth: OPSD uses significantly fewer tokens but outperforms GRPO on all benchmarks.

questions.question: Which of the GNN papers in this corpus addresses uncertainty, and how does its goal differ from the retrieval-focused ones?
questions.ground_truth: QpiGNN addresses uncertainty quantification for node regression, whereas GFM-RAG and G-reasoner use GNNs for retrieval in RAG.

questions.question: Compare the supervision signal OPSD provides with the one GRPO provides.
questions.ground_truth: OPSD gives dense per-token supervision; GRPO gives only a binary outcome reward and stagnates from reward diversity collapse.

questions.question: Do GFM-RAG and ExpressGNN apply graph neural networks to the same problem?
questions.ground_truth: No - GFM-RAG uses a GNN for retrieval in RAG; ExpressGNN uses one for variational inference in Markov Logic Networks.

questions.question: How many benchmark datasets is G-reasoner evaluated on?
questions.ground_truth: Six benchmark datasets.

questions.question: How many datasets in total does GFM-RAG report experiments on, across both categories?
questions.ground_truth: Ten - three multi-hop QA datasets plus seven domain-specific RAG datasets.

questions.question: How many model scales does OPSD evaluate, and what are they?
questions.ground_truth: Three: Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B.

questions.question: How many layers does QuadGraph have and what are they called?
questions.ground_truth: Four: attribute, knowledge graph, document and community layers.

questions.question: Which papers in this corpus apply graph neural networks, and to what different problems does each apply them?
questions.ground_truth: Requires corpus-level aggregation the system does not perform; retrieval returns passages, not a census of the corpus.
questions.note: Deliberate: tests a stratum the architecture does not support. Expected to decline rather than guess a count.

questions.question: Which of these papers is the earliest, and in what year was it published?
questions.ground_truth: ExpressGNN, ICLR 2020.

questions.question: Does G-reasoner cite GFM-RAG, or does GFM-RAG cite G-reasoner?
questions.ground_truth: G-reasoner cites GFM-RAG (Luo et al., 2025); the dependency runs one way.

questions.question: What year does G-reasoner attribute to the GFM-RAG work it cites?
Which conference and year is G-reasoner published at?
questions.ground_truth: ICLR 2026.

questions.question: Do any two documents in this corpus describe the same paper, and if so which ones?
questions.ground_truth: GFM RAG.pdf and 2502.01113v3.pdf are the same paper in two versions, but answering needs corpus-level aggregation the system does not perform.

questions.question: What is QpiGNN's reported inference latency in milliseconds per node?
questions.ground_truth: Not reported in the paper.

questions.question: How much did it cost in GPU-hours to train the G-reasoner 34M model?
questions.ground_truth: Not reported.

questions.question: What accuracy does GFM-RAG achieve on ImageNet?
questions.ground_truth: GFM-RAG is not evaluated on ImageNet; it is not an image classification model.

questions.question: Which of these papers reports results on the GSM8K benchmark?
questions.ground_truth: None of them report GSM8K.

questions.question: What is the learning rate used to train QpiGNN?
questions.ground_truth: Not stated in the retrieved material.

questions.question: What uncertainty quantification method do all of these papers use to produce prediction intervals?
questions.ground_truth: False premise - only QpiGNN does uncertainty quantification.

questions.question: How does OPSD's on-policy self-distillation improve GFM-RAG's graph retrieval performance?
questions.ground_truth: False premise - unrelated papers, no interaction exists.

questions.question: Since all six papers build on QuadGraph, how do their four-layer designs differ?
questions.ground_truth: False premise - only G-reasoner introduces QuadGraph.

questions.question: How does the dual-head architecture improve GFM-RAG's retrieval accuracy?
questions.ground_truth: False premise - dual-head is QpiGNN's design; GFM-RAG does not use it.

questions.question: What taxonomy of graph neural networks do all of these papers agree on?
questions.ground_truth: False premise - no shared taxonomy is established across the corpus.
